# bayesfoRest: Forest Plots for Bayesian Meta Analyses in R <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="200px" />

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

## Overview

bayesfoRest is an R package for creating publication-ready forest plots from Bayesian meta-analyses. It provides a comprehensive solution for visualizing meta-analytic results with support for various effect measures, subgroup analyses, and risk of bias assessments.

## Key Features

- **Bayesian Forest Plots**: Create forest plots from models fitted with brms, bayesmeta, MetaStan, rstanarm, rstan, cmdstanr, bayesma, RoBMA or R2jags
- **Multiple Effect Measures**: Support for OR, HR, RR, IRR, MD, and SMD
- **Density or Boxplot Output**: Show study posteriors as densities or horizontal boxplots
- **Subgroup Analysis**: Built-in support for subgroup meta-analyses
- **Few-Study Safeguard**: `re_min_k` switches to a common-effect model when there are too few studies to estimate tau
- **Risk of Bias Integration**: Incorporate risk of bias assessments (RoB 2, ROBINS-I, ROBINS-E, QUADAS-2, CLARITY, ROB-NMA, PROBAST)
- **Shrinkage Visualisation**: Display shrinkage effects with density plots or point intervals
- **ROPE Support**: Add a Region of Practical Equivalence (ROPE) to plots
- **Model Checking**: Funnel plots, MCMC diagnostics, prior sensitivity and prior dominance checks
- **Extensive Customisation**: Colours, fonts, labels, and layout

## Installation

You can install the development version of bayesfoRest from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("BLMoran/bayesfoRest")
```

## Basic Usage

The examples below use the `binary_outcome` dataset that comes with the
package. First prepare the effect sizes with metafor and fit a model (any
supported backend works; brms is shown here):

```{r model, eval=FALSE}
library(bayesfoRest)
library(metafor)
library(brms)

binary_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = Event_Intervention, bi = Outcome_Intervention_No,
  ci = Event_Control, di = Outcome_Control_No,
  n1i = N_Intervention, n2i = N_Control,
  data = binary_outcome) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sei = sqrt(vi))

model_bin <- brm(
  yi | se(sei) ~ 1 + (1 | Author),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = binary_es,
  prior = prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept) +
          prior(cauchy(0, 0.5), class = sd),
  iter = 4000,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))
```

### Binary Outcome Forest Plot (Odds Ratio)

Tell `bayes_forest()` which columns hold the study name, year and arm-level
data:

```{r example, eval=FALSE}
bayes_forest(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  measure = "OR",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,
  n_int = N_Intervention,
  event_ctrl = Event_Control,
  event_int = Event_Intervention,
  xlim = c(0.1, 3.5)
)
```
![](man/figures/forest_plot_binary.png)

For continuous outcomes, use `mean_ctrl`, `mean_int`, `sd_ctrl` and `sd_int`
instead of the event columns. For time-to-event and rate outcomes, use
`time_ctrl` and `time_int`.

### Boxplots Instead of Densities

`plot_output = "boxplot"` draws each study as a horizontal boxplot. The box is
the interquartile range, the line is the median and the whiskers are the 95%
credible interval. Shrinkage estimates are shown as point intervals.

```r
bayes_forest(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  measure = "OR",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,
  n_int = N_Intervention,
  event_ctrl = Event_Control,
  event_int = Event_Intervention,
  plot_output = "boxplot",
  xlim = c(0.1, 3.5)
)
```
![](man/figures/forest_plot_boxplot.png)

### Add Subgroups

```r
bayes_forest(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  measure = "OR",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,
  n_int = N_Intervention,
  event_ctrl = Event_Control,
  event_int = Event_Intervention,
  subgroup = TRUE,
  subgroupvar = Subgroup,
  xlim = c(0.1, 3.5)
)
```
![](man/figures/forest_plot_subgroup.png)

### Few Studies: `re_min_k`

With only a handful of studies, the between-study heterogeneity (tau) is
poorly identified. Setting `re_min_k` makes this explicit: any analysis (or
subgroup) with fewer than `re_min_k` studies is shown as a common-effect
model, with a message saying so. Leave it as `NULL` (the default) if you would
rather keep the random-effect model and use an informative prior on tau.

```r
bayes_forest(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  measure = "OR",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,
  n_int = N_Intervention,
  event_ctrl = Event_Control,
  event_int = Event_Intervention,
  subgroup = TRUE,
  subgroupvar = Subgroup,
  re_min_k = 5
)
```

```r
bayes_forest(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  measure = "OR",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,
  n_int = N_Intervention,
  event_ctrl = Event_Control,
  event_int = Event_Intervention,
  subgroup = TRUE,
  subgroupvar = Subgroup,

)
```
![](man/figures/forest_plot_rob.png)

```r
  model = model_bin,

  measure = "OR",

  yearvar = Year,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,

```
![](man/figures/forest_plot_rob_legend.png)

### Exclude Studies with High Risk of Bias
```r
bayes_forest(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  measure = "OR",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,
  n_int = N_Intervention,
  event_ctrl = Event_Control,
  event_int = Event_Intervention,
  subgroup = TRUE,
  subgroupvar = Subgroup,
  add_rob = TRUE,
  add_rob_legend = TRUE,
  rob_tool = "rob2",
  exclude_high_rob = TRUE,
  xlim = c(0.1, 3.5)
)
```
![](man/figures/forest_excl_high_rob.png)

### Standalone Risk of Bias Plot

```r
rob_plot(
  data = binary_outcome,
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  rob_tool = "rob2",
  add_rob_legend = TRUE
)
```
![](man/figures/rob_viz.png)

If your data has domain judgements but no overall column, `rob_overall()`
derives one using the tool's rules.

### Overall Plot

```r
overall_plot(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  measure = "OR",
  add_tau = TRUE,
  add_pred = TRUE,
  incl_mu_prior = TRUE,
  incl_tau_prior = TRUE,
  add_null_range = TRUE,
  mu_xlim = c(0.1, 3.5),
  tau_xlim = c(0, 1.5),
  plot_arrangement = "vertical"
)
```
![](man/figures/overall_plot.png)

The dashed lines are the priors, drawn on the same density scale as the
posteriors. They are read from brms and bayesmeta models; for other backends,
pass them with `mu_prior` and `tau_prior` (e.g. `mu_prior = bf_normal(0, 1)`).
With `add_null_range = TRUE` the shaded region defaults to an odds ratio of 0.9
to 1.1; set your own with `null_range`.

### Funnel Plot

```r
funnel_plot(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  measure = "OR",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  yi_col = "yi",
  sei_col = "sei",
  label_studies = TRUE
)
```
![](man/figures/funnel_plot.png)

### MCMC Diagnostics

```r
diagnostics(model_bin)
```
![](man/figures/diagnostics.png)

### Sensitivity Plot

Priors are written with the `bf_*()` helpers, so the same list works whichever
backend the model was fitted with. For the pooled effect use `bf_normal()` or
`bf_student_t()`. For the heterogeneity use `bf_half_normal()`,
`bf_half_cauchy()`, `bf_half_t()`, `bf_exponential()`, `bf_lognormal()` or
`bf_uniform()`, or the empirical priors `bf_turner()` (binary outcomes) and
`bf_rhodes()` (continuous outcomes), which are informative and especially
useful when there are few studies. If the model's backend cannot fit a prior
exactly, you get an error rather than a substitute; `?bf_priors` lists which
backends support which priors.

```r
priors <- list(
  vague = list(
    name = "Vague",
    mu_prior = bf_normal(0, 10),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 1)),
  weakreg = list(
    name = "Weakly Regularising",
    mu_prior = bf_normal(0, 1),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 0.5)),
  informative = list(
    name = "Informative",
    mu_prior = bf_normal(0, 0.5),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 0.3))
)

sensitivity_plot(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  priors = priors,
  measure = "OR",
  rob_var = Overall,
  exclude_high_rob = TRUE,
  incl_common_effect = TRUE,
  add_probs = FALSE,
  xlim = c(0.25, 1.5),
  add_null_range = TRUE
)
```
![](man/figures/sens_plot_no_prob.png)

### Sensitivity Plot with Probabilities

```r
sensitivity_plot(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  priors = priors,
  measure = "OR",
  rob_var = Overall,
  exclude_high_rob = TRUE,
  incl_common_effect = TRUE,
  add_probs = TRUE,
  xlim = c(0.25, 1.5),
  add_null_range = TRUE
)
```
![](man/figures/sens_plot_prob.png)

Publication-bias-adjusted models come from a RoBMA fit: pass it with
`robma_fit = your_robma_fit` and choose the components with `incl_robma`,
`incl_pet_peese` and `incl_selection_weight`.

### ECDF Plots

`ecdf_model_plot()` compares the posterior of the pooled effect across models
for one prior set:

```r
ecdf_model_plot(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  priors = priors["weakreg"],
  measure = "OR",
  rob_var = Overall,
  exclude_high_rob = TRUE,
  incl_common_effect = TRUE,
  xlim = c(0.25, 1.5),
  add_null_range = TRUE
)
```
![](man/figures/ecdf_plot.png)

`ecdf_prior_plot()` compares it across prior sets for one model:

```r
ecdf_prior_plot(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  priors = priors,
  measure = "OR",
  xlim = c(0.25, 1.5),
  add_null_range = TRUE
)
```
![](man/figures/ecdf_prior_plot.png)

### Prior Checks

`prior_dominance()` (shown as a table with `gt_prior_dominance()`) reports how
much the data have updated each prior. `prior_scale_sweep()` and
`tau_scale_sweep()` refit the model over a range of prior scales, and
`plot_prior_scale_sweep()` and `plot_tau_scale_sweep()` plot the results.

```r
prior_dominance(model_bin) |> gt_prior_dominance()

tau_scale_sweep(model_bin) |> plot_tau_scale_sweep()
```

## Dependencies

bayesfoRest depends on several R packages:

- [metafor](https://wviechtb.github.io/metafor/index.html) for meta-analysis preparation (suggested)
- [brms](https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/), [bayesmeta](https://cran.r-project.org/package=bayesmeta), [MetaStan](https://cran.r-project.org/package=MetaStan), [RoBMA](https://fbartos.github.io/RoBMA/) and other backends for Bayesian model fitting (suggested; install the ones you use)
- [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com) for creating tables
- [patchwork](https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com) for combining plots
- [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org) for plotting
- [ggdist](https://mjskay.github.io/ggdist/) for density plotting
- [tidybayes](https://mjskay.github.io/tidybayes/index.html) for tidy workflow
- [dplyr](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org), [tidyr](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org), [purrr](https://purrr.tidyverse.org) for data manipulation
- [paletteer](https://emilhvitfeldt.github.io/paletteer/) for colour palettes
- [fontawesome](https://rstudio.github.io/fontawesome/) for risk of bias icons
- [posterior](https://mc-stan.org/posterior/) for working with posterior draws
- [S7](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/) for risk of bias tool specifications
